title: Android Settings Skills
description: How to reach and change Android system settings reliably.
instructions:
Work down this list and stop at the first step that applies. Opening the Settings app and searching is the LAST resort, not the first move.

1. CHANGE IT DIRECTLY. Some settings never need the Settings app at all: set_volume, set_brightness, set_dnd, set_ringer_mode, toggle_torch and vibrate take effect immediately. Prefer these — they are instant and cannot fail on navigation. Most of them report the previous value; pass that on if it is relevant, and reuse it if you are later asked to change the setting back.

2. JUMP STRAIGHT TO THE SCREEN. For settings you cannot change directly, call open_setting with the matching name (wifi, internet, mobile_data, nfc, bluetooth, location, airplane_mode, battery_saver, display, sound, date_time, language, input_method, storage, accessibility, default_apps, cast). It lands on the exact screen and tells you where the control is — then read_screen and tap it. Do not search for these; you are already there.

3. ASK FIRST FOR RISKY ONES. developer_options, lock_screen, vpn and device_admin change device security or how the phone can be controlled. Use the question tool to get the user's explicit agreement, then call open_setting again with confirmed=true. Never do these silently, even if the request seems to imply it.

4. ONLY THEN SEARCH. If open_setting has no entry for what you need (OEM-specific screens, gesture settings, per-manufacturer battery managers), open the Settings app and use its search: find the search bar or magnifying glass at the top, tap it, then use input_text — do NOT tap the on-screen keyboard key by key. After typing, tap the result with tap or tap_index rather than pressing enter. If the keyboard hides the results, use swipe to reveal what is behind it. Only scroll the Settings home page manually if search itself fails.

When you report back, say what actually happened. If you only opened a screen for the user to finish, say that — do not claim you changed a setting you merely navigated to.
